title: Picking the Right Channels to Market
description: Learn how to evaluate, select, and optimize distribution channels based on customer fit and acquisition cost.

interactions.prompt: What is a "channel" in go-to-market strategy?

options.text: A TV network where you run ads
Any path through which your product reaches customers
A Slack workspace for your sales team
The pricing tier you offer to enterprise buyers

interactions.teachingPreamble: A distribution channel is any route your product takes to reach the end customer. When Shopify launched, it used content marketing, app store partnerships, and a direct sales team  -  each was a distinct channel. Choosing the right mix determines how fast and efficiently you grow.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS startup reports: Google Ads CAC = $320, LinkedIn Ads CAC = $185, Organic SEO CAC = $45, Partner referrals CAC = $90. Monthly budget is $10K. Which insight matters most right now?

options.text: Google Ads is too expensive and should be cut immediately
Organic SEO has the lowest CAC and deserves more investment
LinkedIn is the sweet spot between scalability and cost
Partner referrals should be the only channel used

interactions.prompt: Why is channel-market fit important when choosing distribution channels?

options.text: It ensures your logo looks good on partner websites
It guarantees the lowest possible customer acquisition cost
It matches how your target buyers actually discover and buy products
It means using the most popular marketing channel available

interactions.teachingPreamble: Channel-market fit means your distribution channel matches the buying behavior of your target audience. Atlassian found channel-market fit by selling developer tools through a self-serve website  -  because developers prefer to try before they buy, not talk to salespeople. A mismatched channel wastes money no matter how good your product is.

interactions.prompt: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) is calculated by dividing total ____ spend by the number of new customers acquired in that period.

options.text: Sales and marketing
Product development
Total company operating
Customer support

interactions.prompt: You're launching a B2B accounting tool for small businesses. You can either invest in a direct sales team (higher CAC, faster feedback) or build a self-serve freemium funnel (lower CAC, slower learning). Which do you choose at launch?

options.text: Direct sales  -  early customer conversations shape the product faster
Freemium funnel  -  small businesses won't take sales calls anyway
Split budget 50/50 to test both channels equally
Skip both and rely on word-of-mouth referrals only

interactions.prompt: What is the main risk of relying on a single distribution channel?

options.text: It simplifies reporting too much for investors
Platform changes or cost increases can cripple your entire growth engine
Customers will get bored seeing you in one place
Your competitors will copy your exact channel strategy

interactions.teachingPreamble: Channel concentration risk is real. Zynga built its entire business on Facebook's platform, and when Facebook changed its algorithm in 2012, Zynga lost 80% of its daily active users almost overnight. Smart GTM strategies diversify across 2-3 proven channels while continuously testing new ones.

interactions.prompt: You're a seed-stage B2B startup with a $5K monthly marketing budget. Rank these channel investments from highest to lowest priority: (a) Sponsoring a major industry conference for $4K, (b) Creating SEO-optimized content targeting buyer pain points, (c) Launching a paid LinkedIn campaign at $50/lead, (d) Building a partner referral program with 3 complementary tools.

options.text: Sponsor a $4K industry conference
Create SEO content targeting buyer pain points
Run paid LinkedIn ads at $50 per lead
Build referral partnerships with complementary tools

interactions.prompt: Your top-performing SEO channel just took a hit  -  Google's latest algorithm update dropped your organic traffic by 60%. Your partner referral program is growing but only delivers 20 leads/month. What's your best next move?

options.text: Double down on SEO and wait for traffic to recover
Accelerate partner program and add paid search to bridge the gap
Pause all marketing and focus purely on product improvements
Pivot to outbound cold calling as your primary channel

interactions.priorContext: Previously, you ranked SEO content as your top channel priority and were building a partner referral program. Now a Google algorithm change has disrupted your primary growth engine.
